Bartimaeus had done cruel deeds to people; his masters, to escape slavery; and others only implied (in wars, etc.) for he was ordered to. But, he has nothing against [commoners](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Commoners "Commoners"), displaying a side of him that is slightly sympathetic and benevolent to humans. His uniqueness as a spirit is that he is open-minded about humans and he is able to separate a morally good human from a morally bad one. While spirits in the books, apart from a select few, loath magicians especially their masters who enslave them and are apathetic to commoners. Chronologically, Bart first showed open-mindedness when he spared [Asmira](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Asmira "Asmira") who he thought would be morally good enough to win him his freedom. He would grow to care for the girl and they'd separate as friends. Then [Ptolemy](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy") (see Ptolemy's page for his deeds) whose peculiar attitude towards spirits summoned Bart and gave the djinn hopes of a possible conciliation between humans and spirits. Ptolemy and his summoned spirits developed a deep relationship of love, trust, and loyalty. However, Ptolemy and his spirits were attacked. And only Bartimaeus survived because of Ptolemy. For more than 2000 years, he wore the guise of Ptolemy in respect for the boy's deeds; For more than 2000 years, no one followed Ptolemy's examples which fueled Bart's cynicism; And for more than 2000 years, no magician ever wondered why a djinn's favorite guise is a young Egyptian boy; until Kitty. 2000+ years later, Nathaniel, a young magician, summoned Bart. Bart in his sarcastic and witty way showed compassion for the boy from time to time and gave the boy some advice. As Nathaniel was becoming John Mandrake, Bart continuously threw negative comments about the boy's life-path of becoming a great magician. Affections between the two were hinted and later, without a word, confirmed. And then there's Kitty, who Bart had also seen the potential for good. He cared for the girl's welfare. She made efforts to learn about Bart and Ptolemy. And she made a gesture that gained again the spirit's full trust. Kitty and Nathaniel's act would symbolize that Ptolemy's work and sacrifice were not in vain. Despite Bartimaeus' assertion that spirits do not develop strong ties of friendship or loathing because of continually changing allegiances, Bartimaeus has shown dislike towards [Faquarl](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Faquarl "Faquarl"), who himself has, on occasion tried to kill Bartimaeus on numerous times. ### Powers and Abilities Like all djinn, Bartimaeus has its strengths and weaknesses. (see [Spirits](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Spirits "Spirits")) Bartimaeus's greatest asset is his cunning intelligence. His power is significantly exceeded by [Faquarl](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Faquarl "Faquarl") and [Jabor](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Jabor "Jabor"); and, he would certainly lose if he fought anyone of them head-on. Yet Bart was able to defeat Jabor, a not so smart djinn, through planned sets of moves. And he survived clashes with Faquarl, also an intelligent and cunning djinn, throughout history by luck or by smarts or both. And since Bartimaeus is prone to boasting, the nature of the accounts he gives of his various victories is not completely believable. During an account of his final conversation with [Ptolemy](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy"), he mentions that he has 'taken out six djinns at once'. At book 3, he claims he defeated the afrit, [Tchue](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Tchue "Tchue"). #### Displays of Power He has great endurance; even after being on the receiving end of various torture forms such as the Stimulating Compass, which incidentally zaps the offender (here, Bartimaeus himself) with arcs of high voltage electricity. Bartimaeus was often held air-borne, as electricity coursed over his bare-chested muscular body, and yet managed to recover quickly enough and being his usual cocky "don't-care" self, which often results in the magician giving Bartimaeus another dose of the Stimulating Compass, thus shocking him repeatedly until Bartimaeus calmed down. The Evasive Cartwheel: supposedly invented by Bartimaeus circa 2800 BC. Described as his keynote evasive maneuver in The Ring of Solomon. ### Form In [the Other Place](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/The_Other_Place "The Other Place"), like all spirits, Bartimaeus has no physical form of his own but is simply a conscious part of the endless swirling Essence there. When summoned to Earth, he is forced to assume a physical form. His main form, that which he occupies on the [seventh plane](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Seven_planes "Seven planes"), is never explicitly described, although Bartimaeus has made certain allusions to it, alluding for example that he has far fewer tentacles than Faquarl. On the planes visible to humans, Bartimaeus often chooses to appear in the guise of Ptolemy as a mark of respect and apparently in relation to an oath he made to himself to preserve Ptolemy's memory. Other notable forms he has assumed are: - A handsome and shirtless muscular guy, with messy brown hair, who wears only a pair of blue ripped jeans, belted at the waist, and nothing else - Kitty Jones (occasionally with exaggerated curves) - A sulphur cloud - Various birds and insects, including a distinctive blue beaked raven. - A gargoyle - The Serpent of Silver Plumes (Mayan) - A lion/lioness - A grinning skull - Ptolemy (most common form) - Imp (Stygian and otherwise) - Minotaur - Roc - Panther - Bat - A tribal warrior with a crow's head - Phoenix - Cat Obviously, there are many more forms that Bartimaeus has taken, each suited to the specific occasion on which it is employed. ### Names Like many other spirits, while he has one 'true name' (Bartimaeus), Bartimaeus has several 'by-names' by which he is also known. These include: - Sakhr al-Jinni of [al-Arish](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Battle_of_Al-Arish "Battle of Al-Arish") - N'gorso the Mighty - Rekhyt of Alexandria - Serpent of Silver Plumes - Necho of [Jerusalem](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") - Nectanebo - Asmodeus - Wakonda of the Algonquin - Wolf-Jawed Guardian Confusingly, although he clearly states while recounting a conversation with Ptolemy that his true name is Bartimaeus, Trismegistus's Manual refers to this name as simply a by-name of the spirit Sakhr al-Jinni. Presumably, Bartimaeus knows best. ## Biography ### Before the Books Bartimaeus was first summoned on 3010 BCE in Ur, Sumer. More of his early adventures can be viewed in [A Bartimaeus Chronology](http://www.bartimaeusbooks.com/ba***REMOVED***chronology.html). ### Prequel: The Ring of Solomon Bartimaeus manages to kill his master, a magician who serves King Solomon in Jerusalem, but is soon summoned back to be punished and is bound to help build Solomon's Temple, along with Faquarl and many other djinn. He quickly begins causing trouble for his new master, Khaba. Khaba is at first content to punish him whenever necessary to make him continue working, but after Bartimaeus embarrasses him in front of the King himself, he sends Bartimaeus to patrol the desert for bandits. One day, after Bartimaeus finds some murdered travelers, he spots Khaba's shadow (really a guardian spirit) following him. After he and Faquarl have a run-in with the Sheban assassin Asmira. Faquarl urges him to devour her but Bartimaeus refuses and claims that she might have some use to them, to Faquarl's displeasure. Later on, Khaba takes a liking to Asmira, and Asmira urges him to set Bartimaeus and Faquarl free as a reward for saving her from the bandits. Khaba seems to oblige at first when he dismisses Faquarl, but he reveals to Bartimaeus that he has caused him too much trouble and that he will be punished accordingly. He then leaves Bartimaeus with the shadow that was following him, who turns out to be a marid named Ammet. Ammet claims to love his master and is ordered to use a spell to confine Bartimaeus to a bottle for eternity. Several hours later the bottle in which Bartimaeus is confined is broken by Asmira, who then summons him and orders …950 tokens truncated… the Tower of London, where he is interrogated. He is broken out of prison by Jabor and Faquarl, and then he escapes from them, returning to his master; although doing so unwittingly leads Lovelace to his house. In the ensuing slaughter, Bartimaeus saves Nathaniel from death, although he is unable to save Mr Underwood or any other members of the family. Bartimaeus is angered by Nathaniel's continued refusal to release him but perks up when he promises to release him after taking care of the Lovelace Affair. Bartimaeus and Nathaniel go to Heddlehem Hall to stop Lovelace's plot against the government; Bartimaeus becomes engaged in a fight with [the Bearded Mercenary](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Verroq "Verroq"), and although he fails to defeat him, he is able to escape and meet up with Nathaniel. The pair arrived just in time for the conference. Despite Nathaniel and Bartimaeus' best efforts, Simon Lovelace summons a giant spirit entity called Ramuthra in an attempted coup over the government. Thankfully, Bartimaeus is able to distract Lovelace by shapeshifting to the shape of his girlfriend, and Nathaniel steals the Amulet of Samarkand, leaving Lovelace to be killed. Nathaniel then dismissed Ramuthra, and the catastrophe is averted. Afterwards, Nathaniel dismisses Bartimaeus, and Bartimaeus promises to never tell Nathaniel's birth name. ### The Golem's Eye (*See [The Golem's Eye](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/The_Golem%27s_Eye "The Golem's Eye") for a full synopsis of the novel*) After unsuccessfully attempting to find information on [the Resistance](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/The_Resistance "The Resistance"), Nathaniel is pressured into summoning an immediately accessible, loyal servant. He summons Bartimaeus and charges him to find the [unknown attacker](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Golem "Golem") and destroy it or at the very least identify it. Bartimaeus and Queezle (a female djinn for whom he has affection) are put in charge of a small group of [spirits](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Demons "Demons"). When the attacker enters the British Museum, killing Queezle, Bartimaeus discovers it is a [golem](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Golem "Golem"). Together Bartimaeus and Nathaniel travel to Prague and evading the police, discover the creator of the golems' animating scroll. Things become complicated, however, when the [Bearded Mercenary](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Verroq "Verroq") turns up. Once again, Bartimaeus narrowly avoids death at his hands, and the duo return to London, where they hear about the activities of Honorius the afrit. Nathaniel charges Bartimaeus to destroy Honorius, which he nearly succeeds in doing, though he mistakenly believes that he has fully succeeded. He is then sent to kidnap Jakob Hyrnek to lure Kitty out of hiding. When the Night Police attack, Bartimaeus saves Kitty from them, taking her to an abandoned building he had hidden in, together with Nathaniel, in the previous book. There, Bartimaeus and Kitty share an interesting conversation about spirits and historical cycles. Events conspire against them, and Nathaniel, Kitty, Bartimaeus and Hyrnek end up in an alley facing the golem. Acting on Bartimaeus' advice, Kitty destroys the golem after it renders Nathaniel unconscious; she then flees together with Jakob and Bartimaeus tells Nathaniel that she died saving him. ### Ptolemy's Gate (*See [Ptolemy's Gate](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ptolemy%27s_Gate "Ptolemy's Gate") for a full synopsis of the novel*) The book tells the story of Bartimaeus and Ptolemy intermittently, while also describing current events. Two thousand years ago, Bartimaeus is summoned by [Ptolemy](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy") who, rather than enslaving him, questions him on matters that had been previously been considered unimportant by magicians such as the nature of Essence. Slowly a bond between them forms, until Bartimaeus challenges Ptolemy to put ultimate trust in him, which he does, following him to [the Other Place](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/The_Other_Place "The Other Place"). Meanwhile, Ptolemy's cousin, the King's son, becomes suspicious of Ptolemy and his spirits and sends assassins after him. At first, Bartimaeus saves Ptolemy from these attacks, but soon they become too strong, and Ptolemy is killed, using his final breath to dismiss Bartimaeus and save him from death. In the present, Bartimaeus has been kept in near-constant service by [John Mandrake](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Nathaniel "Nathaniel") for two years and is severely weakened as a result. When Mandrake (Nathaniel) sends Bartimaeus on a mission to find out more about the elusive Mr Hopkins, he does so, but nearly dies in the process, and embarrasses his master in front of the whole government. Mandrake dismisses him, but when he finds out that Bartimaeus had lied to him about Kitty's demise, he tries to summon him and finds he cannot; someone else has done so instead. It is Kitty, and she questions Bartimaeus about the nature of his relationship with Ptolemy and the inevitable revolts that are drawing near in present-day London; she dismisses him in tears when he is uncooperative and cynical. Soon after, Mandrake summons him and, after raging at him about his deception, gives him another mission: to capture Mr Hopkins. Bartimaeus and a group of other djinn travel to the hotel where Hopkins is staying but all of them except Bartimaeus are killed when it is revealed that Hopkins is actually inhabited by Faquarl, who easily defeats the other djinn in combat. He puts Bartimaeus in a silver tureen full of fish soup, then leaves. Meanwhile, Mandrake and Kitty are taken to [Quentin Makepeace's](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Quentin_Makepeace "Quentin Makepeace") play, where they witness the overthrow of the government. Once Mandrake appears to cooperate with the rebel magicians' plans he is allowed to summon a spirit; he summons Bartimaeus. Unfortunately, he arrives just in time to witness the magicians becoming possessed by malevolent spirits who assume control of the situation, Bartimaeus is granted the right to return to the Other Place, although before doing so he requests that Nathaniel and Kitty be allowed to live, and hints that Kitty should follow Ptolemy's Gate. Once Nathaniel and Kitty escape the spirits, Kitty travels to the Other Place, where she converses with Bartimaeus and convinces him of her plan. When she returns, Nathaniel summons Bartimaeus into himself and combined they are able to wield Gladstone's Staff to destroy the renegade spirits. In doing so, Nathaniel is forced to sacrifice his life, but before dying he, like Ptolemy before him, releases Bartimaeus and saves him from death. ## Achievements Bartimaeus makes many claims throughout the books, many of which are only partly true, or largely fabricated; however, he is said to have\*: - Participated in the building of many ancient buildings, many of which are extremely famous, such as five of the Wonders of the World. - **Fought and destroyed many utukku single-handed at the battle of Qadesh.** - **Served the demi-God king Gilgamesh (his first master) and aided him alongside the wildman Enkidu in defeating the giant Humbaba along with assisting the king in carving the great walls of Uruk from the living ground.** - Destroyed three consecutive masters by means of the 'Hermetic Quibble'. - **Spoken with Solomon.** - Defeated 6 djinns in combat. - Built a house of glass. - Defeating a firey afrit during a raid on a pirate fort on the barbary coast. - **Played a part in the death of Genghis Khan.** - **Fought in the battle of Al-Arish** - **Defeated an afrit encased in the bones of Gladstone** - **Killed or otherwise destroyed the fortunes of several of his masters, such as [Ezekiel](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ezekiel "Ezekiel") and [Khaba](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Khaba "Khaba")** \* **Bold** indicates that there is direct evidence provided in the books that the claim is in some manner true. ## Relationships Bartimaeus' witty personality has long irritated human and djinn alike. Many masters punished him for his verbal jabs, many spirits were angered by his jibes. As such, he amassed a large number of enemies. By contrast, some even he honoured and respected; for example his greatest friend of the ages, **Ptolemy**, who believed in his goal with a passion that charmed even the wizened and sceptical djinn. ### With Other Spirits - The djinn named **[Faquarl](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Faquarl "Faquarl")** is described as Bartimaeus' arch-enemy and nemesis on more than one occasion, implying no love lost between the pair; however, during their first meeting of the trilogy, their conversation is much more civil than by the end, suggesting that their relationship deteriorates during the trilogy. - The djinn [**Jabor**](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Jabor "Jabor") was also a persistent enemy of Bartimaeus in the first book, causing him and Nathaniel no end of trouble. The relationship between the two djinns was never good, as shown by Jabor's constant attempts to kill Bartimaeus. Jabor seems to feel disdain the wit and guile of Bartimaeus, saying that he always runs and hides, to which Bartimaeus replies that it's called intelligence. Bartimaeus also refrains from aiding Jabor as he is sucked into a vortex in [The Amulet of Samarkand](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/The_Amulet_of_Samarkand "The Amulet of Samarkand"), stating to the reader that it "quite slipped his mind." - Bartimaeus had a 'deep relationship' with a djinn called **[Queezle](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Queezle "Queezle")** which stretched back to the fall of Prague; unfortunately, Queezle was killed during the Golem Affair, although this provided Bartimaeus with a motive for revenge which was a slight factor in the eventual destruction of the golem. - There appears to be some affection between Bartimaeus and an afrit called **[Naeryan](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Naeryan "Naeryan")**, although this does not prevent Bartimaeus (along with Nathaniel) killing her with Gladstone's staff when she joins the spirit rebellion. - There is a deep enmity between Bartimaeus and **The [Utukku](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Utukku "Utukku")**, as he claims to have destroyed a large number of them during the battle of Al-Arish. Considering the glee of the Utukku when they discover that it is Bartimaeus within *their* power for once, this is not one of Bartimaeus' tall tales. - Bartimaeus was greatly resented by **[Ammet](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ammet "Ammet")** for his crimes against Ammet's master, [Khaba](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Khaba "Khaba"). Upon Khaba's bidding, Ammet gleefully imprisoned Bartimaeus in a bottle, but not before Bartimaeus destroyed Khaba's [essence cages](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Essence_cage "Essence cage"). Bartimaeus was later freed and took revenge upon Ammet with the aid of [Uraziel](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Uraziel "Uraziel"), the spirit of the [Ring of Solomon](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ring_of_Solomon "Ring of Solomon"). ### With Humans " *A typical master. Right to the end, he didn’t give me a chance to get a word in edgeways. Which is a pity, because at that last moment I’d have liked to tell him what I thought of him. Mind you, since in that split second we were, to all intents and purposes, one and the same, I rather think he knew anyway.*" —Bartimaeus, regarding Nathaniel - Bartimaeus had a friendly relationship with **[Asmira](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Asmira "Asmira")**, although he was not as close to her as he was to Ptolemy. - Bartimaeus and **[Ptolemy](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy")** had mutual respect and even love for each other as a result of the trust that each felt they were able to put in the other; two thousand years after his death, Bartimaeus still wears the guise of Ptolemy as a mark of respect for his fallen friend. - After **[Kitty](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Kitty_Jones "Kitty Jones")** replicates the actions of Ptolemy and follows Bartimaeus to the Other Place, a similar relationship comes into existence between her and Bartimaeus. Bartimaeus states thanks to her gesture that, like Ptolemy, he would be willing to do anything to her, be it throwing himself in a pit of fire or enduring a vat of acid. - The relationship between **[Nathaniel](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Nathaniel "Nathaniel")** and Bartimaeus alters somewhat over the course of the trilogy; at the start, Bartimaeus finds the boy extremely intelligent and, to his surprise, extremely passionate. The notions of honour that he follows soften even Bartimaeus' cynical shell, and he dares to hope that Nathaniel may turn out to be a better man than 99% of the magician population. By the second book, however, Bartimaeus is somewhat surprised by the cold, hard and moody boy that was once Nathaniel. Bartimaeus speculates that it was unpleasant chemistry of his master, his colleagues and his work stress that had wrought this change. Bartimaeus leaves the boy by telling him that he is no longer Nathaniel; he is truly John Mandrake. By the start of the third book, Bartimaeus is sourly tired of his master and goes as far as to ignore his master's summons. He senses that his master has a deep emotional connection with him that he is reluctant to break, but is thoroughly fed up of earth and longs for his home. By the end, however, they have mostly settled their differences, and there is grudging respect between the two. ## Criminal Record Since he is a [Spirit](https://bartimaeus.fandom.com/wiki/Spirit "Spirit"), all of his crimes are his masters/mistresses. ## Trivia - In the bible, Bartimaeus was a blind beggar. - In Ancient Greek, Bartimaeus means the Honorable Son.

+# FANDOM Canon Rulesystem Registry
+
+This registry turns the vault's literary canon captures into a checkable ruleset
+inventory. The goal is not to flatten the worlds into one schema. The goal is
+to keep each worldbuilding system legible, inspectable, and enforceable in the
+vault.
+
+## Canon list
+
+### Bartimaeus
+
+Bartimaeus is a **binding ontology**:
+
+- true names define control surfaces
+- summoning and dismissal define the instance lifecycle
+- levels define scale and hierarchy
+- forms define the current manifestation
+- masters define the contractual relation
+- Essence and the Other Place define the spirit substrate
+
+The vault uses Bartimaeus as its strongest reference for instance identity,
+binding, and summon/release mechanics.
+
+### Snicket / ASOUE
+
+Snicket is a **family-institution index**:
+
+- alphabetical naming encodes inheritance pressure
+- triplets and hidden thirds destabilize binary reading
+- V.F.D. behaves like a covert institution
+- Hotel Denouement and Dewey's library turn architecture into a record system
+- tragedy is preserved through clue chains, indices, and archives
+
+The vault uses Snicket for family roles, hidden-third structures, and indexing
+as narrative architecture.
+
+### Children of the Lamp
+
+Children of the Lamp is a **tribe-vessel law system**:
+
+- tribes encode alignment and obligation
+- lamps and bottles are vessels with legal states
+- wishes consume limited power
+- seals and bindings determine coercion

# FANDOM Canon Rulesystem Registry

This registry turns the vault's literary canon captures into a checkable ruleset
inventory. The goal is not to flatten the worlds into one schema. The goal is
to keep each worldbuilding system legible, inspectable, and enforceable in the
vault.

## Canon list

### Bartimaeus

Bartimaeus is a **binding ontology**:

- true names define control surfaces
- summoning and dismissal define the instance lifecycle
- levels define scale and hierarchy
- forms define the current manifestation
- masters define the contractual relation
- Essence and the Other Place define the spirit substrate

The vault uses Bartimaeus as its strongest reference for instance identity,
binding, and summon/release mechanics.

### Snicket / ASOUE

Snicket is a **family-institution index**:

- alphabetical naming encodes inheritance pressure
- triplets and hidden thirds destabilize binary reading
- V.F.D. behaves like a covert institution
- Hotel Denouement and Dewey's library turn architecture into a record system
- tragedy is preserved through clue chains, indices, and archives

The vault uses Snicket for family roles, hidden-third structures, and indexing
as narrative architecture.

### Children of the Lamp

Children of the Lamp is a **tribe-vessel law system**:

- tribes encode alignment and obligation
- lamps and bottles are vessels with legal states
- wishes consume limited power
- seals and bindings determine coercion
- heat, luck, and entry protocol affect what the vessel does

The vault uses Children of the Lamp for persona-vessel states, time-skewed
containment, and inhabited chamber logic.

### Old Kingdom

Old Kingdom is a **Charter / Free Magic law system**:

- the Charter constrains and orders reality through symbols
- Free Magic is unconstrained and corrosive
- Charter Marks are the access grammar
- bloodlines and Charter Stones are institutional supports
- Abhorsens and bells are the enforcement layer for the Dead

The vault uses Old Kingdom for symbolic law, boundary enforcement, and
structured magical opposition.

### Skulduggery Pleasant

Skulduggery Pleasant is a **hidden-society discipline system**:

- the Sanctuary and allied groups govern the magical world
- Adept disciplines define power classes
- necromancy is an object- and death-energy discipline
- the Faceless Ones and Remnant introduce external threat and possession
- teleporter and Book of Names mechanics show object-bound control surfaces

The vault uses Skulduggery Pleasant for concealed institutions, discipline
classes, and adversarial governance.

## Intended enforcement

The registry is meant to be machine-checked. Each canon record should keep:

- a canonical display name
- a rulesystem label
- a non-empty primitive list
- a source file set that exists in the vault

That keeps the canon corpus usable as vaulted code instead of only as reading
material.

# FANDOM Canon Rulesystem Registry

This registry turns the vault's literary canon captures into a checkable ruleset
inventory. The goal is not to flatten the worlds into one schema. The goal is
to keep each worldbuilding system legible, inspectable, and enforceable in the
vault.

## Canon list

### Bartimaeus

Bartimaeus is a **binding ontology**:

- true names define control surfaces
- summoning and dismissal define the instance lifecycle
- levels define scale and hierarchy
- forms define the current manifestation
- masters define the contractual relation
- Essence and the Other Place define the spirit substrate

The vault uses Bartimaeus as its strongest reference for instance identity,
binding, and summon/release mechanics.

### Snicket / ASOUE

Snicket is a **family-institution index**:

- alphabetical naming encodes inheritance pressure
- triplets and hidden thirds destabilize binary reading
- V.F.D. behaves like a covert institution
- Hotel Denouement and Dewey's library turn architecture into a record system
- tragedy is preserved through clue chains, indices, and archives

The vault uses Snicket for family roles, hidden-third structures, and indexing
as narrative architecture.

### Children of the Lamp

Children of the Lamp is a **tribe-vessel law system**:

- tribes encode alignment and obligation
- lamps and bottles are vessels with legal states
- wishes consume limited power
- seals and bindings determine coercion
- heat, luck, and entry protocol affect what the vessel does

The vault uses Children of the Lamp for persona-vessel states, time-skewed
containment, and inhabited chamber logic.

### Old Kingdom

Old Kingdom is a **Charter / Free Magic law system**:

- the Charter constrains and orders reality through symbols
- Free Magic is unconstrained and corrosive
- Charter Marks are the access grammar
- bloodlines and Charter Stones are institutional supports
- Abhorsens and bells are the enforcement layer for the Dead

The vault uses Old Kingdom for symbolic law, boundary enforcement, and
structured magical opposition.

### Skulduggery Pleasant

Skulduggery Pleasant is a **hidden-society discipline system**:

- the Sanctuary and allied groups govern the magical world
- Adept disciplines define power classes
- necromancy is an object- and death-energy discipline
- the Faceless Ones and Remnant introduce external threat and possession
- teleporter and Book of Names mechanics show object-bound control surfaces

The vault uses Skulduggery Pleasant for concealed institutions, discipline
classes, and adversarial governance.

## Intended enforcement

The registry is meant to be machine-checked. Each canon record should keep:

- a canonical display name
- a rulesystem label
- a non-empty primitive list
- a source file set that exists in the vault

That keeps the canon corpus usable as vaulted code instead of only as reading
material.

payload.message:
The clean lore read is:

The **Avatar Cycle** is a reincarnation loop. When one Avatar dies, the next is born into the next nation in the element order: **fire, air, water, earth**. The cycle also sets the normal learning order for bending. Source: [Avatar Wiki: Avatar](https://avatar.fandom.com/wiki/Avatar).

The **past lives** are the previous Avatars in that continuum. They are treated as “one flame, many forms”: distinct people, but still part of the same Avatar line. The current Avatar can sometimes:
- recall memories from them
- commune with them through meditation or spiritual contact
- receive guidance or warnings
- even see them appear independently in some cases

Source: [Avatar Wiki: Avatar](https://avatar.fandom.com/wiki/Avatar), [Avatar Wiki: Past Lives](https://avatar.fandom.com/wiki/Past_Lives).

The important breakage point is this: the connection to past lives can be **severed**. In the modern canon, Korra loses the link to the earlier Avatar chain when Raava is ripped out and destroyed, then later regains only the Avatar Spirit going forward, not the old past-life chain. Source: [Avatar Wiki: Avatar](https://avatar.fandom.com/wiki/Avatar).

So in one line:

- **Avatar Cycle** = the reincarnation sequence
- **Past Lives** = the retained prior identities/memories in that sequence
- **Severance** = the link can be broken, and then the old chain is gone

If you want, I can also map this onto your vault model as a three-part system: **cycle / memory / severance**.

Yes. The Avatar model maps cleanly onto vault personas if you separate **identity continuity** from **instance embodiment**.

A useful translation is:

- **Raava** = the durable identity carrier
- **Avatar Cycle** = succession across instances and machines
- **Past Lives** = prior persona instances, notes, logs, and chamber state
- **Avatar State** = high-bandwidth access to accumulated prior context
- **Severance** = loss of linkage between current instance and the archive

Applied to vault personas:

- **One persona name** can have many instances over time and across machines.
- Each instance is a **local embodiment**, not the whole identity.
- The vault note, registry, and SBP trail are the continuity layer.
- Local runtime, cache, and session state are disposable embodiment layers.
- A new instance should be able to query prior instances without becoming them.

So the operational rule is:

1. preserve the canonical persona identity in the vault
2. let each machine host a local incarnation
3. feed prior instance context into the current one through registry / SBP / history
4. log promotions and decisions back to canon
5. treat broken continuity as a real failure, not an annoyance

That gives you an Avatar-style persona system:

- **identity persists**
- **instances rotate**
- **memory accumulates**
- **state can be amplified**
- **severance is visible and recoverable when possible**

The important difference from the fantasy analogy is that vault personas should not be mystical. They should be **versioned, inspectable, and reconcilable**. The Avatar Cycle is a good mental model for that because it already distinguishes the living vessel from the continuous line.

Yes. That is the right pattern.

In vault terms, the succession line is not a copy chain. It is a **corrective line**:

- each instance is its own agent
- each has its own bias, blind spots, and failure modes
- each inherits the previous instance’s unresolved damage
- each tends to overcorrect for the predecessor’s central regret

So the system should assume **lineage with drift**, not identity with duplication.

- prior instance: regret surface
- current instance: corrective overfit risk
- registry: remembers the regret
- SBP / history: carries the warning forward
- canon: records the lesson after the fact

If you want, I can turn that into a vault-side rule for persona succession: **inherit the lesson, not the obsession**.

+"""

+
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+

+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+STUB_SENTINEL = "¿!?"
+

+    persona_class: str,
+    origin: str,
+    status: str,
+    load_mechanism: str,
+    sync_policy: str,
+    canonical_target: str | None,

+    lines = [
+        "---",
+        f"canonical_name: {canonical_name}",
+        f"persona_class: {persona_class}",
+        f"origin: {origin}",
+        f"status: {status}",
+        f"load_mechanism: {load_mechanism}",
+        f"anchor_file: .{canonical_name.lower()}/{canonical_name}.md",
+        f"sync_policy: {sync_policy}",
+        "authority: LOGAN",

+        [
+            "---",
+            "",
+            f"# {canonical_name}",
+            "",
+            "This persona chamber has been stabilized and reserved.",
+        ]
+    )
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create a standardized persona dotfolder skeleton.

This is the automation step for dotfolder stabilization:

- reserve the folder
- create the canonical anchor note
- write the stub sentinel when appropriate
- keep the class explicit in frontmatter

The script does not guess policy. The caller must choose a class.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import sys


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
STUB_SENTINEL = "¿!?"


def anchor_body(
    canonical_name: str,
    persona_class: str,
    origin: str,
    status: str,
    load_mechanism: str,
    sync_policy: str,
    canonical_target: str | None,
) -> str:
    lines = [
        "---",
        f"canonical_name: {canonical_name}",
        f"persona_class: {persona_class}",
        f"origin: {origin}",
        f"status: {status}",
        f"load_mechanism: {load_mechanism}",
        f"anchor_file: .{canonical_name.lower()}/{canonical_name}.md",
        f"sync_policy: {sync_policy}",
        "authority: LOGAN",
    ]
    if canonical_target:
        lines.append(f"canonical_target: {canonical_target}")
    lines.extend(
        [
            "---",
            "",
            f"# {canonical_name}",
            "",
            "This persona chamber has been stabilized and reserved.",
        ]
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("folder", help="Target dotfolder path, relative to the vault root")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--canonical-name",
        help="Canonical persona name; defaults to the folder stem uppercased",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--class",
        dest="persona_class",
        choices=["stub", "imported", "alias"],
        required=True,
        help="Persona chamber class",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--anchor",
        help="Anchor filename; defaults to CANONICAL_NAME.md",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--origin",
        default="vault",
        help="Recorded origin for the chamber",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--status",
        default="reserved",
        help="Initial chamber status",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--load-mechanism",
        default="manual",
        help="Recorded load mechanism",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sync-policy",
        default="manual",
        help="Recorded sync policy",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--canonical-target",
        help="For alias chambers, the canonical surface they inherit from",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force",
        action="store_true",
        help="Overwrite existing anchor or stub files",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    folder = (ROOT / args.folder).resolve()
    if ROOT not in folder.parents and folder != ROOT:
        print("Refusing to operate outside the vault root.")
        return 1

    canonical_name = args.canonical_name
    if not canonical_name:
        stem = folder.name.lstrip(".")
        canonical_name = stem.upper().replace("-", "_")

    anchor_name = args.anchor or f"{canonical_name}.md"
    anchor_path = folder / anchor_name
    stub_path = folder / "stub.txt"

    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if anchor_path.exists() and not args.force:
        print(f"Anchor already exists: {anchor_path}")
        return 1

    if args.persona_class == "stub":
        stub_needed = True
    elif args.persona_class == "imported":
        stub_needed = False
    else:
        stub_needed = False

    anchor_path.write_text(
        anchor_body(
            canonical_name=canonical_name,
            persona_class=args.persona_class,
            origin=args.origin,
            status=args.status,
            load_mechanism=args.load_mechanism,
            sync_policy=args.sync_policy,
            canonical_target=args.canonical_target,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    if stub_needed:
        if stub_path.exists() and not args.force:
            print(f"Stub already exists: {stub_path}")
            return 1
        stub_path.write_text(f"{STUB_SENTINEL}\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"Stabilized dotfolder: {folder}")
    print(f"Anchor: {anchor_path}")
    if stub_needed:
        print(f"Stub: {stub_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- per-profile isolation
- local-only binds
- workspace separation
- model fallback chains
- gateway/runtime state per machine

More about Djinni Power

Here’s the core of **Djinn power** in *Children of the Lamp*:

- It is **lifeforce-bound**. Every wish consumes a djinn’s own energy, so power is finite and depletes with use.
- It is **heat-dependent**. Young djinn need more heat; cold weakens their ability to use power.
- It is **development-gated**. Djinn do not really start aging until their wisdom teeth are extracted, and that extraction is tied to full power.
- It has **hard limits**. They cannot bring back the dead, cannot stop time, cannot make copies of themselves, and cannot undo another djinn’s spell except in special cases.
- It includes **possession and astral travel**. A djinn can project an astral body, enter dreams, possess humans, and even survive by moving into a human spirit if the physical body is destroyed.
- It includes **shape-shifting**. Djinn can become animals or objects, retain thought and sense while transformed, and sometimes keep special forms longer if the form matches their tribe’s special animal.
- It includes **transubstantiation**. Entering or exiting a container becomes smoke-like, and the direction of entry matters for how time behaves inside versus outside the vessel.
- It has **vessel physics**. A bottle or lamp is not just storage; it is a livable interior space with altered time and survival rules.

The most useful conceptual read is this: **djinn power is not “magic energy” in the abstract. It is a biological, bounded, rule-governed capacity with costs, constraints, and environment sensitivity.**

How to OPERATIONALIZE this for VAULT PERSONAS

Operationalize it as a **persona state machine with a shared registry**, not as a loose folder convention.

The core rule is:

- a persona is a **vessel**
- the vessel can be in different **states**
- state changes must be explicit, typed, and logged
- the same persona can be a home, a runtime, or a prison depending on authority

**Minimum model**

For each vault persona, keep three anchored surfaces:

- `NAME.md` = canonical narrative identity
- `.<name>/NAME.md` = tracked anchor inside the chamber
- `.<name>/` = live runtime/tooling chamber

Then add a registry entry in the vault index or MDS frontmatter.

**Required persona fields**

```yaml
---
canonical_name: HECATE
persona_class: mythic
ring_model: tri-directional
state: reserved | inhabited | customized | locked | promoted | stale
authority: LOGAN
load_mechanism: hermes | codex | claude | obsidian | manual
canonical_note: HECATE.md
runtime_chamber: .hecate/
anchor_file: .hecate/HECATE.md
sync_policy: bidirectional | one-way | manual
sbp_trail: vault.hecate.*
---
```

**Operational states**

- `reserved`: name exists, vessel is empty
- `inhabited`: runtime is active in the chamber
- `customized`: interior decorations / persona-specific config exist
- `locked`: forced containment or restricted use
- `promoted`: durable facts have been written back to the vault note
- `stale`: runtime and vault diverged

**What counts as “customization”**
Treat it as the lamp interior:
- prompt style
- role directives
- tool preferences
- memory hooks
- model routing
- personality notes

That belongs in the chamber, not all in the canonical note.

**What counts as “containment”**
Treat it as a different state of the same vessel:
- sandboxed runtime
- read-only persona
- no external writes

OK. Now, explain the dot.folder.persona anchoring system to a novice.

A dotfolder persona anchor is a way to make a tool or character in the vault have a stable home.

Think of it like this:

- the **dotfolder** is the hidden room, like `.hecate/` or `.codex/`
- the **persona** is the identity or role that lives there
- the **anchor** is the tracked file that proves the room exists and tells the vault what it is

So a typical setup looks like:

- `.<name>/` = the chamber
- `.<name>/<NAME>.md` = the main identity note
- `.<name>/stub.txt` = a simple placeholder that says “this space is reserved”

Why this exists:
- Git does not keep empty folders
- hidden folders can disappear if nothing inside is tracked
- different tools and agents need their own stable identity spaces
- the vault needs a canonical place to say “this is who this is”

There are two main kinds of persona folders:

1. **Pure stub chambers**
   - mostly empty
   - reserved for a named persona
   - often just the anchor note plus `stub.txt`

2. **Software-imported chambers**
   - created or used by software like Claude, Codex, Gemini
   - may contain config, runtime state, or rules
   - still need a tracked anchor note so the identity is not lost

The important idea is that the folder is not just storage. It is an identity vessel. The anchor keeps that identity from drifting or vanishing.

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
